skill.name: debugging-toolkit-smart-debug
skill.description: Guides structured debugging, root cause analysis, instrumentation planning, and post-fix validation for software issues.
skill.summary: Structured debugging workflow for triage, diagnosis, fixes, and validation.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All three static findings were adjudicated as false positives because the flagged patterns occur in markdown prose or an illustrative TypeScript example. No semantic evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden abusive behavior was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line contains a markdown inline path reference to resources/implementation-playbook.md, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. It is instructional prose and does not execute a command.
The flagged backticks open a fenced TypeScript example with illustrative debugging pseudocode. There is no executable Ruby shell backtick pattern in the skill.
Lines 132-133 contain success criteria bullets such as tests passing and no performance regression. They do not perform or instruct network reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Complex failures are hard to triage when logs, traces, and code evidence are scattered. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured diagnosis, fix planning, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Extracts errors, reproduction steps, affected components, environments, and failure patterns from user input.
Ranks debugging hypotheses with evidence, probability, falsification criteria, and testing approach.
Selects debugging strategies for local, production, intermittent, and observability-driven issues.
Recommends instrumentation points, logpoints, spans, and production-safe diagnostics.
Structures root cause, fix proposal, validation plan, and prevention steps.
limitations: Does not connect to Sentry, DataDog, or other platforms by itself.
Relies on the user or agent environment to provide logs, traces, and code context.
Example observability calls are illustrative and require real project integrations.
Cannot prove a fix without running the relevant tests and monitoring checks.

use_cases.title: Triage a Production Incident
use_cases.description: Diagnose an active service failure by combining stack traces, metrics, deployment context, and ranked hypotheses.

use_cases.title: Investigate Intermittent Bugs
use_cases.description: Compare failing and passing conditions, select instrumentation points, and design falsification tests for inconsistent behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan a Fix Review
use_cases.description: Evaluate proposed changes with impact, risk, rollback, and validation steps before release.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize an Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to triage this error. Identify the likely component, severity, missing information, and first debugging steps: [paste error].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a single error message.

prompt_templates.title: Rank Root Cause Hypotheses
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this stack trace, logs, and reproduction path. Produce three ranked hypotheses with evidence, falsification criteria, and tests: [context].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate diagnosis with multiple evidence sources.

prompt_templates.title: Design Safe Instrumentation
prompt_templates.prompt: For this production issue, propose low-risk logpoints, traces, metrics, and sampling rules that can confirm or reject each hypothesis: [incident details].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced production debugging with observability constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Create an End-to-End Debug Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a complete debug plan for this incident. Include observability queries, code paths, fix options, rollback strategy, validation, and prevention: [full context].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced incident analysis from triage through prevention.

output_examples.input: A checkout service times out for five percent of production users after the latest deployment.
output: Issue summary: checkout timeouts affect a small production cohort after the latest deployment.
Likely causes: external payment latency, N+1 database queries, or changed timeout configuration.
Next steps: compare traces before and after deployment, inspect slow spans, add query count instrumentation, and validate with canary metrics.

output_examples.input: A local test fails intermittently when run with the full suite but passes alone.
output: Issue summary: the failure depends on shared suite state or timing.
Likely causes: stale cache, leaked mock state, shared database rows, or race conditions.
Next steps: isolate order, randomize runs, add state checks around setup and teardown, and create a regression test.

best_practices: Provide stack traces, deployment timing, logs, metrics, and reproduction steps before asking for root cause analysis.
Ask for falsification criteria so each hypothesis can be tested or rejected.
Validate fixes with tests, performance comparison, and monitored rollout data.
anti_patterns: Do not accept a single cause without evidence from logs, traces, tests, or code.
Do not add broad debug logging in production without sampling, access controls, and removal plans.
Do not skip rollback and monitoring steps for fixes deployed to users.

faq.question: Does this skill run debugging commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides methodology and analysis prompts. Any commands or integrations must be executed by the agent or user environment.

faq.question: Can it debug production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide observability data, deployment context, symptoms, and constraints from the production environment.

faq.question: Does it require Sentry or DataDog?
faq.answer: No. It references common observability tools, but the workflow can use any logs, metrics, or traces you provide.

faq.question: How does it handle intermittent bugs?
faq.answer: It recommends comparing failing and passing paths, adding targeted instrumentation, and defining falsification criteria.

faq.question: Can it write the final code fix?
faq.answer: It can help plan and review a fix, but implementation depends on project code, tests, and permissions.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive logs?
faq.answer: Review and redact secrets or personal data before sharing logs with any AI tool or marketplace skill.
